**Summary:** The audit freshness gate (skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py `_check_audit_freshness` / `_compute_content_fingerprint`) keys freshness on the whole-repo git HEAD sha. ANY commit to the repo — even one touching files unrelated to the work item — changes HEAD, invalidates the content fingerprint, and forces a full two-phase re-audit. This caused a real false re-audit: NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U was audited "Ready to close: No" (AC5 partial), the content fingerprint was byte-identical on re-audit, yet an operator `/skill:audit` invocation re-ran the full pipeline (twice, dry-run and persisted), and the final persisted verdict flipped to "Ready to close: Yes" purely from model judgment variance on the same unverifiable AC — no new evidence. A freshness gate that actually asserted "the work is in HEAD" would have returned the stored verdict.

**Desired behavior:** freshness must be decided per work item, not per repo. If NO file touched by the work item has changed since the work was committed, the stored audit verdict stands — no re-audit, no model calls. If any touched file changed, the audit is stale and re-runs.

**User stories:**
- As an operator running `/skill:audit <id>` on an item whose work files are unchanged, I want the stored verdict returned in seconds so unrelated repo commits never trigger an expensive re-audit.
- As an operator, I want the gate to be strict about the work item itself: any change to files the item touched (or to its ACs/description/Key Files) must invalidate freshness.

**How to determine "files touched by the work item":**
1. Commits referencing the work item ID: `git log --all --grep=<id>` and/or the commit messages recorded on the work item comments (implement skill already records commit hashes). The union of files in those commits = touched files.
2. The Key Files section of the work item description (already parsed by `_extract_key_files`).
3. Fallback: if touched-file set cannot be determined (no commits recorded, git unavailable), fail open and re-run the pipeline (current behavior).

**Suggested approach (strict-mode fingerprint):** extend `_compute_content_fingerprint` to a payload of {touched-file set (paths + per-path current git blob hashes or latest commit touching each path), description_hash, key_files} instead of the bare repo HEAD sha. On freshness check, recompute per-path state; equality => fresh. Document trade-offs: the gate is no longer fail-open-cheap the same way, and tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. Unity batch runs rewriting ProjectSettings, see Nova AGENTS.md pitfall #4) must be tolerated — e.g. exclude known tool-artifact paths or accept that they invalidate freshness (safe direction: stale => re-run is never wrong, only wasteful).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] (AC1) Freshness gate decides freshness from the work item touched-file set, not the bare repo HEAD sha: a commit touching only unrelated files does NOT invalidate a stored audit with an unchanged fingerprint
- [ ] (AC2) Any change to a file in the touched-file set invalidates freshness and re-runs the pipeline
- [ ] (AC3) Work-item description/AC/Key Files changes still invalidate freshness (existing behavior preserved)
- [ ] (AC4) Touched-file set resolution falls back to fail-open (re-run pipeline) when it cannot be determined (no recorded commits, git unavailable)
- [ ] (AC5) Tool-artifact rewrites (e.g. ProjectSettings churn from Unity batch runs) are handled explicitly — either excluded from the touched-file comparison or documented as always-invalidating with a test
- [ ] (AC6) Unit tests cover: unrelated-commit freshness (AC1), touched-file change invalidation (AC2), description-change invalidation (AC3), and fail-open fallback (AC4)
- [ ] (AC7) Re-audit of NV-0MSP7P2PN009FT9U at unchanged state returns the stored verdict without re-running the pipeline (regression scenario from this issue)
data.title: Audit freshness gate: re-audit only when files touched by the work item changed

# Intake Brief — Ship skill: Discord release notification

**Work item:** SA-0MSQ6K7Z1002H14Z — Ship skill: send Discord message with release details + changelog on successful release (`feature`, priority `medium`)

## Problem statement

When the ship skill completes a successful release (dev → main), there is currently no automatic notification; operators must poll GitHub/worklog to learn what shipped. We want the ship skill to post release details — including the changelog — to a Discord channel on every successful release.

## Users

- **Operator / release manager (human)** — wants a record of each release in a Discord channel without manually checking GitHub.
  - *User story:* "As an operator, when a release ships successfully, I want a Discord message with the version, tag, PR link, and changelog posted to a channel I configure, so my team sees what shipped without checking GitHub."
- **Team members watching the Discord channel** — consume the release summary passively.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1 — After a **successful, non-dry-run** release (verified landed on `origin/main`), the ship skill posts a Discord message to the configured channel containing: released version, git tag (`vX.Y.Z`), release date, PR URL, and the new version's changelog section from `CHANGELOG.md`.
- AC2 — Config resolution: the per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` `discord.webhook_url` takes precedence over the global fallback (`~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`, same key). If neither is set, no message is sent and the release completes normally (logged, not an error).
- AC3 — Notification is **non-blocking**: a failed or slow webhook POST logs a warning and does not change the release exit code; a release that already landed is never failed by a notification failure.
- AC4 — The webhook payload respects Discord limits (embed description ≤ 4096 chars); an over-long changelog is truncated with an ellipsis marker.
- AC5 — Unit tests cover: config precedence + skip-when-unset, changelog extraction/truncation, payload shape, and non-blocking failure behavior. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- AC6 — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (ship skill `SKILL.md` and its reference docs, including config schema and behavior).

## Constraints

- Code lives in the **global agent skill** `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/` (not the repo); per-project config lives in the repo's `.worklog/config.yaml`.
- No new runtime dependencies: Node.js 18+ is already a prerequisite; use the built-in `fetch` for the webhook POST.
- The webhook URL is a **secret** (contains an auth token) — must not be committed to the repo; the global fallback file lives outside the repo. Config schema must be documented as sensitive.
- Must not alter existing gating, exit codes, or the Code Freeze contract.
- Notification is a post-release concern — it must run only after release-merge verification (never on `--dry-run` or failed releases).

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` orchestrates the release: 5 gates → `merge-dev-to-main.sh` (bump version, generate `CHANGELOG.md`, merge, tag `vX.Y.Z`, push, PR) → wait PR merge → `syncDevWithMain()` → `verifyReleaseMerge(version)` → `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease(version)`.
- `generate-changelog.js` writes `CHANGELOG.md` at repo root with sections `## vX.Y.Z (YYYY-MM-DD)` and Features / Bug Fixes / Other categories.
- Ship currently reads **no** config file; the per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` (projectName, prefix, autoExport, autoSync) is the established config convention.
- No existing Discord/webhook integration in the agent infra or this repo; no `DISCORD_*` env vars set.

## Desired change

Add a new post-release step in `run-release.js` (after `verifyReleaseMerge()` succeeds, alongside the close-work-items step) that:

1. Resolves the webhook URL: per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` → `discord.webhook_url`, falling back to global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` → `discord.webhook_url`. Unset → log info, skip, proceed.
2. Extracts the new version's changelog section from `CHANGELOG.md`.
3. Builds a Discord embed payload (version, tag, date, PR URL, changelog description truncated to ≤ 4096 chars).
4. POSTs to the webhook via built-in `fetch`; on any failure logs a warning and returns non-blocking (release exit code unchanged).
5. Dry-run / failed releases never trigger a notification.

New module `discord-notify.js` (config resolution, changelog extraction, payload build, send) with injectable fetch for tests; new unit tests under the skill.

## Key Files:

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — add Step 8.5: call `sendReleaseNotification()` after merge verification succeeds (non-blocking).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/discord-notify.js` — **new**: webhook URL resolution (project → global), changelog section extraction + truncation, embed payload builder, non-blocking `fetch` POST.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/SKILL.md` — document the notification behavior, config schema (`discord.webhook_url`), and non-blocking semantics.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — update reference docs (schema, hook point).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/tests/test_discord-notify.js` — **new**: unit tests (config precedence, skip-when-unset, truncation, payload shape, non-blocking failure).
- `.worklog/config.yaml` (per-project) / `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (global) — config schema consumed (webhook URL is secret — document gitignore/redaction).

## Related work

- `LP-0MSQ0NTMO00577UJ` — "ship skill getCandidateItems(): 'set -o pipefail' fails on dash..." (prior ship-skill maintenance; same skill, adjacent scripts).
- `LP-0MSQ0NI7K009UDE8` — "Release v0.1.13 (dev → main)" (example ship usage/evidence of release flow).
- No existing work item covers release notification or Discord integration (searched: discord, release notification, ship skill).
- Automated find-related report (inserted into item description by the skill) surfaced three low-relevance keyword matches: `LP-0MN8LU516006M2SN` (Co-residency runtime support), `LP-0MQP3Q8DN0047J1H` (Qwen3 reasoning_content fix), `LP-0MRCU7PTG005VVD4` (Content-Encoding gzip header) — matched on generic words (config/channel/release/skill); none are actionable related work.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — secret leakage:** webhook URL committed to a repo. *Mitigation:* document as sensitive; prefer the global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` (outside repos); AC2 covers precedence so a repo can override but needn't store the secret.
- **Risk — notification latency/flakiness:** network hiccup hangs the release. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout on the POST; non-blocking warning on failure (AC3).
- **Risk — Discord rate limits / message size:** >4096-char changelog or 429 responses. *Mitigation:* truncation (AC4); treat 429/5xx as a logged warning (AC3).
- **Assumption — message content:** version, tag, date, PR URL, and changelog section are the "details of the release" requested; no changelog section found → send without changelog (or skip changelog field) rather than fail.
- **Scope-creep guard:** extra ideas (e.g., notify on *failed* releases, Slack/email adapters, rich per-item links) are recorded as separate work items, not added here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1:** "Where should the Discord channel be configured? (a) per-project `.worklog/config.yaml`; (b) global config `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml`; (c) both — global default + per-project override?"
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(c)" — per-project with a global fallback. Final accepted answer: per-project `.worklog/config.yaml` `discord.webhook_url` with global `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` fallback. Prior answers: none changed. Research: ship skill reads no config today; `.worklog/config.yaml` is the established per-project convention (projectName/prefix); `~/.pi/agent/` is the global agent-config home (auth.json, models.json, settings.json) — no existing global YAML config, so `~/.pi/agent/config.yaml` is a new, natural location.
- **Q2:** "What Discord integration mechanism? (a) Webhook URL in config; (b) bot token + channel ID."
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(a)" — webhook URL. Final accepted answer: webhook URL (a webhook is bound to one channel; no bot/channel-ID plumbing needed). Research: no prior Discord integration exists in the repo or agent infra (grep: webhook/discord → only LLM session recordings and node_modules READMEs).
- **Q3:** "If the Discord message fails to send, should the release (a) still succeed — log a warning (non-blocking); (b) be treated as a release failure (blocking)?"
  - **Answer (rgardler, interactive):** "(a)" — non-blocking warning. Final accepted answer: notification failure never fails an already-landed release; warn and continue. Research: release flow already treats post-merge steps non-blockingly (close-work-items step is non-blocking); consistent with that precedent.

## Problem

Global skills (intake, plan, implement, audit, etc.) provided by this project are static and cannot be extended per-project without modifying the global skill files directly. There is currently no mechanism to customize or extend global skills with project-specific behavior.

Each global skill looks in `.pi/skills_extensions/<skill-name>/` for two optional files:
- `SKILL_PREFIX.md` — executed after gating steps, before the first actionable step
- `SKILL_POSTFIX.md` — executed after the final step completes

This convention allows per-project customization of global skill behavior while keeping the core skills untouched.

# Problem statement

When the implement skill encounters a work item that has already been implemented (e.g. the skill detects a commit where the work was completed but the item is in a wrong state/stage, or an audit identifies gaps in what was done), it should review the most recent audit report, fix any identified gaps inline, and proceed — rather than blindly re-implementing or silently skipping.

## Users

- **Agent executing `/skill:implement <id>`**: needs to handle the "already completed" case deterministically without manual intervention or blind re-implementation.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Detect "already implemented"** — the implement skill recognizes when the work has already been completed (e.g. via commit history, status/stage mismatch, or an audit report indicating prior completion).
2. **Review audit report** — when already implemented is detected, fetch/review the most recent audit report for the item (`/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
3. **Close gaps inline** — if the audit reveals gaps (unmet ACs, failing tests, missed requirements), fix them inline as part of the current item's implementation (option b per intake clarification, 2026-08-13) — NOT by creating new work items.
4. **Skip if clean** — if the audit shows no gaps, report the summary and skip further implementation (no re-work).
5. **Update documentation** — the implement skill's `SKILL.md` is updated to describe this new step and its logic.

## Constraints

- Changes are scoped to `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and corresponding doc hygiene tests.
- No new work items should be created for gaps — they are closed inline.
- Follow the existing implement skill structure (add a numbered step, consistent formatting).

## Existing state

The implement skill has no logic to detect when a work item has already been implemented. It proceeds through all steps regardless, which can lead to redundant work or missed gap remediation when an item's state/stage is out of sync with its actual implementation status.

## Desired change

Add a new step in the implement skill (between Step 3.1 "Definition gate" and Step 4 "Create a worktree") that:
1. Checks whether the item has already been implemented
2. If yes: reviews the latest audit report, identifies gaps, and fixes them inline
3. If no: proceeds to the normal workflow

## Risks & assumptions

- **Detection signal ambiguity** — "already implemented" must be driven by the implement skill's own output (it reports completion with a commit hash), not inferred from status alone; document the exact detection trigger in the skill.
- **Audit staleness** — the most recent audit report may predate later fixes; reuse a fresh audit (same guidance as existing Step 3: reuse a recent audit, else `/skill:audit <work-item-id>`).
- **Scope creep in inline gap-closing** — large gaps discovered via audit are potential new work items; keep inline fixes minimal and record extra opportunities as linked work items (discovered-from), not scope.
- **Dependency on audit output format** — logic reads the audit report; keep the reading step aligned with how the audit skill persists reports (`audit_report_<id>.md`).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Add the new step with detection logic and audit review procedure
- `tests/test_implement_skill_doc_hygiene.py` — Ensure doc hygiene tests still pass

## Related work

- SA-0MSAS108O009DYKT — audit skill must write audit report files with unique names
- SA-0MPGU5QG40040AWS — Move recent-audit bootstrap into implement skill
- SA-0MPMGES67002AP0Z — Implement per-child audit loop in Ralph

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What counts as 'already implemented'?" — Answer (operator): option d — the implement skill itself sometimes reports the work is already completed and points to a commit hash; in that situation the item is either (a) completed but in the wrong state/stage, or (b) a problem with the implementation was identified in an audit. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.
- Q2: "What does 'close them' (the gaps) mean?" — Answer (operator): option b — fix the gaps inline as part of the current item's implementation, then proceed to in_review. No new work items for gaps. Source: interactive reply, 2026-08-13.

## Problem statement

The audit runner auto-approves work items as "Ready to close: Yes" when `_extract_acs` returns the zero-AC sentinel (`["No acceptance criteria defined."]`) because it injects a hard-coded placeholder with `"verdict": "met"`. This creates a false-positive approval vector whenever an AC heading doesn't match the regex.

## Users

- **AI agents** running audits on work items (Ralph, AMPA) — expect the audit to accurately reflect AC verification status.
- **Operators** relying on "Ready to close: Yes" as a gating decision — assume ACs have been machine-verified.
- **User stories**:
  - "As an operator, I want the audit to never auto-approve an item with unverified ACs."
  - "As an AI agent, I want the audit to flag when AC extraction fails so I can review the item manually."

## Acceptance criteria

1. When `_extract_acs` returns the zero-AC sentinel, the runner emits a warning-level result and sets `Ready to close: No` (not Yes).
2. Existing items with valid AC headings still produce `Ready to close: Yes` (no regression on the happy path).
3. Unit test: `_extract_acs` sentinel path yields warning verdict.
4. Related documentation updated (code comments, any wiki/docs for the audit pipeline).
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Must not change the sentinel string returned by `_extract_acs` (backward compatibility with other callers).
- The fix is localized to the sentinel-handling branch in the audit runner (~line 5753).
- Should not require changes to the audit result schema (add `warning` level to existing verdict enum if needed).

## Existing state

- `_extract_acs` returns `["No acceptance criteria defined."]` on heading mismatch.
- The runner checks for this sentinel and injects `{"text": "No acceptance criteria defined.", "verdict": "met"}` (hard-coded placeholder).
- This produces "Ready to close: Yes" with zero ACs actually verified.
- Phase 2 deep analysis correctly detects the mismatch (separate safeguard) but the Phase 1 hard-coded sentinel still produces met verdict.

## Desired change

When the sentinel is detected, replace the hard-coded `{"verdict": "met"}` with a warning-level result (e.g. `{"verdict": "warning", "text": "ACs could not be extracted — verify item description uses a recognized heading format"}`). Ensure the overall verdict cannot be "Ready to close: Yes" when any result is warning-level.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Sentinel handling branch (~line 5753)
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — Add unit test for warning verdict on sentinel

## Related work

- SA-0MSM66WAQ001E0AX — audit_runner _extract_acs misses bold headings (source of discovery)
- SA-0MSJLC8XA00178YD — audit_runner AC extractor misses parenthetical headings (merged sibling fix)
- SA-0MSA843FV008V88P — _extract_acs fails on colon header (resolved, same root cause)

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q**: Should the zero-AC sentinel produce a `warning` verdict or a different handling (error/flag)? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: New `warning` verdict level. Source: code inspection — `warning` fits between `met` and `unmet` in severity.
- **Q**: Should Phase 1 or Phase 2 detect the sentinel path specifically? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: Phase 1 sentinel detection (~line 5753) is the primary fix point; Phase 2 already has a separate safeguard (detects 0 machine-verified ACs vs. description ACs). Source: code inspection of audit_runner.py.
- **Q**: Does this need to be a breaking schema change or can `warning` be additive? — **Answer (agent-inferred)**: Additive — `warning` is a new enum value, backward-compatible. Source: code inspection — verdicts are string-based.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption**: The hard-coded placeholder at line 5753 is the sole place where `"verdict": "met"` is injected for the zero-AC sentinel. Other callers (child AC extraction at lines 4013, 4064) already skip processing when sentinel is detected — they do not produce a "Ready to close" verdict.
- **Risk**: Downstream consumers (Ralph, AMPA) may not yet handle a `warning` verdict level. Mitigation: additive enum value, not breaking; consumers that only check `met`/`unmet` will continue to work, treating `warning` conservatively.
- **Risk**: Adding "Ready to close: No" for sentinel paths may change audit results for existing items. Mitigation: these items already have a latent false-positive; the warning is a correction, not a regression.
- **Scope creep risk**: Consideration of auto-approving only when ACs are "sufficient" (count thresholds, content quality) is out of scope — this fix only addresses the sentinel→met path.

## Summary

Redirect all git-based audit operations (`_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, `_resolve_working_tree_hash`, `_compute_content_fingerprint`) to resolve against the worklog-derived owning project root instead of the launch cwd.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Git pieces target the owning project.** When the runner resolves an owning project root from the worklog (explicit `--worklog-dir` parent → prefix-to-sibling scan), `_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` resolve git against that root — **not** the launch cwd.

2. **Undeterminable ownership aborts.** When the owning project root cannot be determined (no `--worklog-dir`, unknown item prefix, no sibling match), the runner aborts with a clear error before any phase runs — it must not fall back to the launch cwd's repo for git-derived content.

3. **No regression for owning-project launches.** Launching from inside the owning project (standard path) and from a worktree of the owning project (same git repository) continues to work; a worktree launch still resolves git to the worktree checkout (never the `--worklog-dir` parent's main checkout), so worktree-only changes and the worktree branch HEAD stay correct.

## Implementation Details

**Approach: Pass `cwd` parameter to subprocess calls for git commands.**

The fix is to inject the owning project root as the `cwd` parameter when running git commands in the affected functions:

- `_git_changed_files(runner)` — modify calls to pass `cwd=str(git_root)` in `subprocess.run` (or wrap the runner to inject `cwd` for git commands).
- `_repo_index(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_resolve_audited_head(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_resolve_working_tree_hash(runner)` — same treatment.
- `_compute_content_fingerprint(runner)` — relies on the above, automatically fixed.
- `_build_file_scope_manifest(work_item, ac_results, runner)` — relies on `_git_changed_files` and `_repo_index`, automatically fixed.

**Recommended implementation strategy:**

Option A: Create a `cwd_aware_runner` wrapper function that prepends `-C <root>` to git commands, replacing `_default_runner` in the git-related calls. This is the simplest surgical change.

Option B: Modify `_default_runner` to accept an optional `cwd` parameter and create a `cwd_aware_runner` closure that pre-binds it. Update all git-related call sites to use `cwd_aware_runner(owning_root)` instead of `_default_runner`.

**Recommendation: Option A** — prepend `-C <root>` to git commands. It's a one-line change per function and avoids modifying the subprocess call signature.

```python
def _cwd_aware_runner(git_root: Path):
    """Return a runner function that prepends `-C <git_root>` to git commands."""
    def _run(cmd: Sequence[str]) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        if cmd and cmd[0] == "git":
            cmd = ["git", "-C", str(git_root)] + list(cmd[1:])
        return _default_runner(cmd)
    return _run
```

**Abort on undeterminable ownership (AC2):**

In `cmd_issue()` (around line 5377), after resolving `owning_root`, if it is `None`, abort with a clear error message before any git operations run. The existing `_verify_launch_context` currently fails open (returns `None` when ownership is undeterminable); this fix turns the abort into the git layer's responsibility.

**Worktree semantics (AC3):**

Reuse the existing `_same_git_repository` logic (line 767). When `owning_root` is resolved and the launch cwd is the same git repository (via `_same_git_repository`), use the launch cwd as the git root. Otherwise use the resolved `owning_root`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_git_changed_files` (:2953), `_repo_index` (:2983), `_resolve_audited_head` (:1348), `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (:1080), `cmd_issue` (5377+).

The audit skill's Phase 1 merge gate (_integrate_into_dev in skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, ~lines 6099-6109) unconditionally runs 'npm run build' after merging the item's work into an integration worktree (build -> test -> commit order per AGENTS.md). For a repo without package.json / build tooling (e.g. docs-only repos such as AI_Hell), this fails with ENOENT and the gate reports 'Merge gate blocked: integration failed: build failed' -> 'Ready to close: No', demoting the item to open/plan_complete — even though the git merge itself succeeded (rc=0) and the change is valid.

User story: As an operator auditing a docs-only work item in a repo without build tooling, I want the audit merge gate to skip/soften the build step so valid changes can pass Phase 1 without the workaround of committing+pushing to dev first.

Impact: any docs-only item in a repo without build tooling cannot pass the audit merge gate when the work is not yet in dev. Workaround (used for AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V): commit + push to dev FIRST, then audit — _verify_merged_in_dev detects the work already in origin/dev and fails open without attempting the build.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Have an audited work item whose commits are NOT yet in origin/dev.
2. Run the audit on a repo with no package.json (e.g. a docs-only GDD repo).
3. Observe the Phase 1 merge gate fail with 'build error'/'build failed' despite the merge succeeding.

Suggested fix: make the build step conditional on the integration worktree having package.json (or a configured build command, e.g. .pi/test-config.json buildCommand), or record a non-blocking note when no build tooling exists. Mirror the conditional-skip approach already applied to the implement skill's run_build() (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1) and run_tests() (SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

Acceptance criteria:
1. Audit Phase 1 integration succeeds for a repo with no package.json and no build tooling; the build step is skipped and recorded as evidence (non-blocking note), not a failure.
2. Audit Phase 1 still runs 'npm run build' and fails the gate when a package.json with a build script exists and the build fails.
3. Existing merge-gate tests (skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_merge_gate.py and related) remain green; a new test covers the no-build-tooling case.
4. Behavior is consistent with the implement skill's conditional build/test skip conventions (SA-0MSM6JHG9002CZA1, SA-0MSN4AXIQ007IZG2).

The implement skill's final end-of-session report step references a report script at a path that does not exist in this repository.

## Problem

The audit runner's merge gate (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`) extracts candidate commit SHAs from work-item descriptions and comments using the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b`. This regex incorrectly matches decimal numbers that happen to be composed entirely of hex digits (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` from a test failure message). The numeric sequence after the decimal point (`2329094824319696`, `231051271500847`) is treated as a valid commit SHA, causing false-positive merge-gate failures.

**Example:** A failing test with the error:
```
expected 0.23290948243196963 to be less than or equal to 0.2310512715008475
```
produces candidate commits `2329094824319696` and `231051271500847` from the audit runner, which then fail to integrate into `dev` because they are not real commit SHAs.

## Root Cause

File: `.pi/skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, function `_resolve_item_integration_evidence`, line ~6119:

```python
for m in re.finditer(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

The `\b` word boundary does not prevent matching within decimal numbers. The sequence `0.23290948243196963` is parsed as a decimal literal, but the substring `2329094824319696` (16 hex chars) passes the 7-40 char hex check.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Audit no longer extracts decimal numbers as commit SHAs:** The regex in `_resolve_item_integration_evidence` must not match numeric sequences that are part of decimal literals (e.g., `0.23290948243196963` → no SHA extracted; `2329094824319696` → no SHA extracted).

2. **Valid commit SHAs are still extracted:** The fix must not break extraction of legitimate commit SHAs:
   - Full 40-hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd3cc78f415afca198930339f2138bed218`)
   - Short 7-39 hex SHAs (e.g., `2c15ebd`, `abc1234`)
   - SHAs in commit messages, WL comment text, and work-item descriptions

3. **Commit SHAs prefixed by `#` (GitHub-style) are still extracted:** `#2c15ebd` or `sha=2c15ebd` patterns should still be detected (the `\b` boundary handles `#` as a non-word character, so the hex sequence is still matched).

4. **All existing audit tests pass:** No regression in the existing audit test suite (`/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/audit/tests/`).

5. **New test coverage:** Add a test that verifies decimal numbers are not extracted as commit SHAs, and a test that verifies valid SHAs in various formats (full, short, GitHub-style) are still extracted.

## Suggested Fix

Replace the regex `\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b` with one that excludes decimal-point-adjacent sequences. Options:

**Option A (negative lookbehind for dot):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<!\.)\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?!\.)", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This uses `(?<!\.)` to ensure the match is not preceded by a decimal point, and `(?!\.)` to ensure it is not followed by one.

**Option B (explicit non-digit-dot context):**
```python
for m in re.finditer(r"(?<![0-9.])\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b(?![0-9.])", desc, re.IGNORECASE):
```

This is more aggressive — it excludes any sequence preceded or followed by digits or dots.

**Option C (split on dots first, then match):**
Preprocess the text: `text.replace('.', ' ')`, then apply the original regex. This is simpler but could break SHAs that happen to be adjacent to dots in unusual contexts (unlikely but possible in commit messages).

**Recommended:** Option A — targeted fix that only excludes decimal-point adjacency, preserving all other behavior.

## Impact

- **Scope:** Single function in `audit_runner.py` (`_resolve_item_integration_evidence`)
- **Risk:** Low — the change is a regex refinement; behavior is identical for all real commit SHAs.
- **Test coverage:** Existing audit tests cover SHA extraction from descriptions and comments; add a test for decimal exclusion.

## Related Work

- N/A — this is a bug in the audit skill's core merge-gate logic.

# Pane title status indicator on skill completion

## Problem statement

When a skill (intake, plan, implement, audit, …) finishes, the operator
cannot tell at a glance whether the pane's work-item session ended cleanly,
needs their attention, or failed. The herdr pane title currently shows only
the dispatch context (e.g. `Manually triggered intake`); the end-of-session
state must be surfaced in the pane title itself.

## Users

- **Operator (producer)** watching a grid of herdr panes: wants a zero-click
  visual signal of which sessions are done, need attention, or failed —
  without opening each pane.

Example user stories:

- "As an operator, when a skill completes cleanly I want a green tick at the
  start of the pane title so I can see it finished."
- "As an operator, when a skill completes but left information for my
  attention I want an orange warning so I know to look at it."
- "As an operator, when a skill cannot complete I want a red no-entry sign
  so I know to intervene."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: When a work-item skill finishes and produces a final report, the herdr
  pane title (label) for the current pane is updated with a status prefix:
  ✅ (or `Done`) when all ACs are met and no substantive producer content
  exists; ⚠️ (or `Note`) when the skill completed but the report contains
  substantive content for the producer's attention; 🚫 (or `Attention`) when
  the skill cannot complete (any unmet/partial/adjusted AC verdict, or
  abort/failure).
- AC2: The prefix is prepended to the existing pane title (e.g.
  `✅ Manually triggered intake`); no colour/ANSI is embedded in the label;
  the update is idempotent (re-running does not stack prefixes).
- AC3: Text fallbacks `Done` / `Note` / `Attention` are used when emoticons
  are not possible (reusing the report's existing `--no-icons` /
  `WL_NO_ICONS=1` mechanism).
- AC4: On skill abort or failure (including abort paths such as
  `intake.py abort`, `implement.py abort`, audit-runner aborts), the pane
  title is set to the red state regardless of whether a final report is
  produced.
- AC5: The update fails gracefully outside a herdr pane (no `HERDR_ENV`,
  `HERDR_PANE_ID`, or herdr CLI unavailable): no crash, no error surfaced to
  the skill run.
- AC6: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, and all
  related documentation is updated (SKILL.md reports, tests for the new
  helper).

## Constraints

- Not a pi extension — the update is a call to the herdr CLI/API
  (`herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane id from
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var; herdr ≥ current installed version).
- Trigger is skill completion (end-of-session report render), not the agent
  harness lifecycle.
- Status is derived from the final report's content: AC verdicts
  (met/unmet/adjusted/partial), Producer Actions, Notes.
- Orange = "audit passed but there is information for the producer's
  attention (not necessarily actions, and certainly not when the next action
  is the standard next action in the workflow)" — i.e. substantive content
  beyond the routine workflow next step.
- Colour requirement dropped for text fallbacks: plain `Done`/`Note`/
  `Attention` prefixes, no colour coding.
- Emoji-vs-text fallback follows the existing report convention
  (`--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1`), so both modes stay consistent.

## Existing state

- Every work-item skill ends by rendering a canonical report via
  `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` (report skill, SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S),
  passing AC verdicts, producer actions, notes and next action.
- herdr panes carry a `label` field shown as the pane title, set via
  `herdr pane rename <pane_id> <label>`; current pane is identified by the
  `HERDR_PANE_ID` env var (present in pi sessions launched via herdr; also
  `HERDR_ENV=1` and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`).
- `render_report.py` already supports `--no-icons` / `WL_NO_ICONS=1` for
  bracketed-text fallbacks — a precedent for the emoticon/text switch.

## Desired change

- Add a small shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py`) that, given a
  status (`done` | `note` | `attention`) and the current pane context,
  prepends the corresponding prefix (✅/⚠️/🚫 or Done/Note/Attention) to the
  existing pane label via the herdr CLI, idempotently.
- Integrate the helper into `render_report.py`: after the report is rendered,
  derive the status from the supplied AC verdicts, producer actions and notes
  and update the pane title (done/note states; red when any AC verdict is not
  met).
- Hook the red state into abort paths (`intake.py abort`, `implement.py
  abort`, audit runner abort/exit paths) so failures always surface red even
  without a final report.
- Fail open when not in a herdr pane or herdr CLI is missing.

## Key Files

- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — derive status from report inputs
  and call the pane-title helper after rendering.
- `skill/shared/herdr_pane.py` (new) — shared herdr CLI wrapper: resolve
  current pane, read existing label, prepend status prefix idempotently.
- `skill/intake/scripts/intake.py` — abort command sets red pane state.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — abort path sets red pane state.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — abort/failure exits set red pane
  state.
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` + `skill/report/tests/test_render_report.py` —
  document and test the status derivation and pane update.

## Risks & assumptions

- **herdr CLI availability:** assume herdr is installed and the pane env vars
  are set in agent panes (true today — pi sessions launched via herdr carry
  `HERDR_ENV`/`HERDR_PANE_ID`). Fail-open behaviour (AC5) mitigates drift.
- **Existing pane title truncation:** herdr truncates long labels to ~60
  chars (`MAX_PANE_TITLE_LENGTH`); the prefix plus existing label must fit
  within the limit — the helper should truncate the combined string the same
  way to keep the title valid.
- **Scope creep:** wiring red-state into *every* skill's abort path is broad;
  the helper centralises the logic so each abort site is a one-liner. Extra
  opportunities (e.g. coloured labels in the herdr UI itself) are recorded as
  follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Verdict vocabulary:** `adjusted`/`partial` verdicts count as "not fully
  met" → red; `met` only → eligible for done/note.

## Related work

- SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S — "Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting
  via helper report skill": the report renderer this feature extends.
- ContextHub herdr (sibling repo `packages/herdr`): `pane rename`, pane
  titles (`pane-title.ts`, WL-0MSJ4E8UA005KG9Y), agent-state protocol.
- find-related matches (repo): `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`,
  `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — the
  abort/failure paths that must surface the red state; no directly-related
  open work items.

- Q: "Should this live in the SorraAgents repo as a reusable extension, or be a built-in feature in the pi-coding-agent?" — Answer (user): "It is not a pi extension, it is a call to the herdr CLI/API." Source: interactive reply (intake session).

## Intake Brief: Multi-agent audit/test coordination to break deadlocks

## Work item
**SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF -- When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing**

## Problem statement

When multiple agents run concurrently (herdr-dispatched implement/plan/audit panes plus manual sessions), audits and test runs contend for the same scarce host resources (local LLM slots, audit concurrency slots, CPU) and end up blocking one another. Two mechanisms interact to create a livelock/starvation pattern: (1) the herdr downtime worker only dispatches any work -- including audits -- after the local LLM has been **continuously idle >=60s with >=2 free slots**; (2) the audit runner **fails fast (0s wait)** when the host-wide audit semaphore is saturated, returning `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts. Under sustained agent traffic the idle gate never opens, so audits starve; in the rare dispatch windows, concurrent audits may still collide and fail-fast, keeping items `in_review` indefinitely. Tableau-Card-Engine currently shows 28 items in `in_review` -- several 1000+ hours old (up to 4178h) -- with only 15 audit dispatches ever recorded and one audit running 8+ hours. A coordination mechanism is needed so audits proceed with bounded, prioritized concurrency independent of a strict "all traffic quiet" gate.

## Users

- **Concurrent agent herd** (herdr instances + pi panes on the same machine) running implement/plan/audit sessions -- they block on audits of their completed items.
- **Audit skill consumers** -- every completed/item-in-`in_review` work item needs a timely audit verdict to progress/close.
- **Operator (rgardler)** -- watches the worklog; a deadlocked herd produces no visible progress and wasted LLM spend.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No fail-fast re-queue under load (north star):** under sustained concurrent agent/LLM traffic, audits no longer return `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts as the *common* outcome; when the ceiling is momentarily saturated, audits wait on a bounded queue (or equivalent) rather than failing immediately. Verification: run N >= 3 concurrent audits against a busy host; zero concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts; all audits persist real verdicts.
2. **Bounded audit turnaround (realistic start):** an `in_review` item is audited within N hours (N to be tuned) of entering that stage while multiple agents are active. Verification: seed/observe items entering `in_review` under concurrent load; 95th-percentile time-to-audit <= N. Note: turnaround is bounded within dispatch windows; the gate-opening frequency is the hard throughput ceiling (see AC3 amendment).
3. **Idle-gate decoupling for audits (amended):** *within any dispatch window*, audit dispatch/progress no longer requires a strict continuous LLM idle window; audits proceed under high agent traffic (bounded by the host-wide audit semaphore), while non-audit dispatch may retain a gentler gate. Note: the idle gate itself is unchanged (see SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 follow-up); this AC is satisfied by the bounded-queue mechanism ensuring audits proceed without fail-fast once a dispatch window opens.
4. **Priority ordering:** among queued/waiting audit candidates, `critical` items are audited before `high`, then age/FIFO; no item is bypassed indefinitely. Verification: deterministic ordering observed in logs/tests; the 4178h-old backlog drains.
5. **No regression to existing guards:** per-item `in_progress` claim guard, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight, lease/leader machinery, and test-cache read-only consumption all continue to work unchanged (see Constraints). **All related documentation updated** (audit skill reference, process_semaphore, AGENTS.md coordination section, downtime-dispatcher doc if touched). **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Single-machine scope (v1) matches herdr's current leader-election/lease model; no new network service.
- Preserve the cross-process flock semaphore primitive (no stale locks); extend semantics (bounded wait/priority/queueing) rather than replace wholesale.
- The dispatcher cannot know a work item's weight before dispatch -- fine-grained coordination belongs in the skills (audit/test) where concurrency is actually consumed; dispatcher changes should be minimal and only where they unblock (e.g., audits not gated on full idle).
- Must not destabilize working coordination machinery: leader lease (5-min TTL), 30-min check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups.
- Keep test execution cheap: the per-repo test cache (2h TTL) already dedupes suite runs; do not regress read-only cache consumption by audits/implement/ship.

# Audit Staleness Race: Post-Persist Comment Bumps updatedAt Past auditedAt

## Headline Summary

A race condition causes passed audits to display a stale icon (⏳) when a comment is added after `wl audit-set`, because the `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` call bumps `updatedAt` past the 60-second freshness window relative to `auditedAt`.

## Problem Statement

When `wl audit-set` persists a passed audit, it sets `auditedAt` to the current time. If any subsequent command (e.g., `wl comment add`) calls `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()`, the `updatedAt` timestamp advances. The `isAuditFresh()` check in `icons.ts` compares `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60000` ms — so a comment added more than 60s after the audit makes `isAuditFresh` return `false`, causing the TUI and selection lists to show a stale icon (⏳) instead of the ready icon (✅).

## Users / User Stories

- **Developer using `wl audit`**: After passing an audit and seeing ✅, a subsequent comment should not invalidate the audit result display.
- **Operator reviewing work items**: The selection list and TUI should accurately reflect audit freshness, not be confused by post-audit comments.
- **Automated agents (pi)**: Agent comments added as part of audit-close workflows should not cause false stale indications.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1**: Persisting a passed audit then immediately adding the audit-result comment does NOT make `isAuditFresh` return false — passed audits retain the ✅ icon in selection lists and the stage display icon past the 60s buffer.
- **AC2**: Skill/docs contract updated — `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and/or `skill/implement/SKILL.md` explicitly orders `wl comment add` **before** `persist_audit.py` / `wl audit-set`, or states that the audit report itself is the record and no separate post-persist comment is needed.
- **AC3**: Fix preserves existing guarantees — `needsProducerReview`-only flips still preserve `updatedAt`, content-fingerprint freshness still works, and normal (non-audit) comments still bump `updatedAt`.
- **AC4**: Regression test coverage — test that `wl audit-set` followed by `wl comment add` within the audit flow does not regress to stale display, or that the runner/list helper correctly reports fresh when comment precedes audit.

## Constraints

- No behavior change for non-audit comments — they must still bump `updatedAt`.
- Do not regress runner re-audit / child-audit freshness logic.
- The 60s staleness buffer for non-audit contexts is unchanged.
- Content-fingerprint freshness (SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT) must continue to work.

## Existing State

- `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:310` checks `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60000`.
- `stageDisplayIcon()` in `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:333` returns `auditStaleIcon(true)` instead of `auditIcon(true)` when fresh check fails.
- `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` is called in `createComment()` (database.ts:3369) and `update()` for content changes (database.ts:1296).
- `needsProducerReview`-only updates do NOT bump updatedAt (database.ts:1299) — this is the precedent we must preserve.

## Desired Change

Ensure the audit-result comment is part of the persisted audit — not a separate post-persist write that invalidates freshness.

**Option A (ordering contract)**: Any final "Audit passed / Ready to close: Yes" comment must be added **before** `persist_audit` / `wl audit-set` so that `auditedAt ≥ updatedAt` after persistence.

**Option B (atomic bundle)**: Bundle the comment text into the audit `rawOutput`/`auditText` atomically so no second `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` follows the audit persist.

## Key Files

- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `createComment() → touchWorkItemUpdatedAt()` (line 3369), `update()` metadata vs content bump (line 1299)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` (line 310), `stageDisplayIcon()` (line 333)
- `packages/shared/src/theme.ts` — mirror of icon logic
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — `persist_audit()` function
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — freshness gates (`_check_audit_freshness`)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` / `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — persistence and close ordering docs

## Related Work

- **WL-0MTEZ5EK5002RXXD** — ContextHub Leader lease zombie fix (observed failure example: auditedAt 13:49:12, updatedAt 13:51:09, comment delta 117s)
- **WL-0MSN6ZCTN0027U2R** — needsProducerReview must not invalidate audit (precedent for preserve-updatedAt)
- **SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT** — Content fingerprint / persist-write tolerance
- **SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4** — audit_runner parent flow loops re-triggering child audits
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** — Eliminate wasteful re-audits

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk**: Changing `touchWorkItemUpdatedAt` behavior for audit comments may affect downstream consumers that rely on `updatedAt` tracking. **Mitigation**: Scope change narrowly to audit-result comments only.

## Summary

`audit_runner.py issue|batch --do-not-persist` currently skips **all** persistence, including the `auditedAt` timestamp. A successful dry-run validation (`Ready to close: Yes`) therefore leaves `auditedAt` stale. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:250`) stays `false`, so Herdr's selection list / DOWNTIME audit tier correctly re-queues the item as a stale-audit candidate and shows the ⏳ stale-passed state.

Observed on 2026-09-01 with `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV`: validated with `--do-not-persist --force` (`Ready to close: Yes`, deep analysis completed) but stored audit remained `2026-08-11T05:13:22Z` while `updatedAt` had advanced to `2026-09-01T18:33:14Z` (delta ~21 days via `herdr-downtime` claim + comments). Herdr was correct to show "out of date" — the dry-run never refreshed the freshness signal. Manual `wl audit-set` was required to make `updatedAt == auditedAt` and restore `isAuditFresh: true`.

## Problem

- `--do-not-persist` is documented as a dry run but gives no freshness guarantee; operators assume a passing validation will clear the stale flag, but it does not.
- Help text (`audit_runner.py:10656`, `10781` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) says only "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" — does not explain the Herdr staleness consequence nor the intended dry-run semantics.

## User story

As an operator running `audit_runner.py --do-not-persist` for a dry-run validation, I want a passing validation to still refresh the audit freshness timestamp so Herdr no longer shows the item as out of date, while the full raw report remains not persisted; the flag's help should make this contract explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Freshness on dry-run success:** When `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` (and `batch --do-not-persist` for each drained item) completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item's `auditedAt` is atomically updated to `now` (`updatedAt == auditedAt` in the same txn, `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` pattern) with `auditResult`/`readyToClose` reflecting the verdict, **without** persisting the full `rawOutput` markdown. `isAuditFresh` must be `true` immediately after, and `wl list --stage in_review --json` must show `auditedAt == updatedAt` and `isAuditFresh: true` (Herdr shows ✅ not ⏳ and excludes from audit tier). When the verdict is `Ready to close: No` / `partial` / failure, `auditedAt` is **not** bumped (fail-closed — a failed dry-run must not clear staleness).
2. **Help text updated:** `--do-not-persist` help on both `issue` and `batch` subparsers (and the `SKILL.md` flag table / persistence procedure) is updated to state: dry-run — full audit report is not stored, but on `Ready to close: Yes` the audit freshness timestamp (`auditedAt`/`auditResult`) is still persisted so Herdr/DOWNTIME treat the item as freshly audited; omit the flag to persist the full report. The previous terse "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" is replaced.
3. **No regression for full persist:** Without the flag, behavior is unchanged — full report + `auditedAt`/`auditResult` persisted atomically and lifecycle transitions (`completed`/`in_review` etc.) still apply. With the flag, lifecycle transitions still apply (flag does not suppress status/stage changes).
4. **Tests:** Unit/cli tests cover the new contract: (a) `--do-not-persist` + `Yes` bumps `auditedAt`/`auditResult` but leaves `rawOutput` empty/absent; (b) `--do-not-persist` + `No` does not bump; (c) help text contains the freshness/dry-run wording (mirrors `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` pattern for SKILL.md validation).
5. **Docs:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` persistence section and runner flag docs updated to match the new flag semantics.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` (dry-run left Herdr stale, required manual `wl audit-set` to recover).
- Implementation hint: reuse the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes|no` path (sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in one txn) for the dry-run success case, passing summary but omitting `--raw-output`/`--audit-file` so `rawOutput` stays null. Do not call `wl update --audit-text` afterwards (that would bump `updatedAt` past `auditedAt + 60s` and re-stale).
- `batch` subcommand should apply the same rule per-item in the drain loop.
- Consider whether a new flag (e.g. `--truly-do-not-persist`) is needed for the rare case where even freshness must not be touched; default should be the freshness-preserving dry-run.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` — effort-and-risk SKILL.md output path (the stale-audit observation)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:isAuditFresh` — `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:selectAuditCandidate` / `isAuditFresh` — audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10656,10781` — flag definition
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py:495` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` note

# Test skill --type parameter with local CWD extension (SA child of SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0)

## Problem

The global `test` skill currently only runs the **full** test suite. There is no way to select a lighter test type during implementation or audit without running the full 15-min suite. Projects like Tableau Card Engine already define fast profiles (unit ~seconds, smoke ~2m, dev ~3.5m, full ~15m) in `AGENTS.md`, but the skill has no typed entry point to invoke them.

A parallel effort (SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 "Local skill extensions for global skills") will allow any global skill to be extended locally via CWD convention. The test skill must consume that extension mechanism so per-project test strategies are defined **locally** in the consuming repo, not hardcoded in SorraAgents.

## Users

- **Producer / agent running `/skill:test`** — wants `unit` during implementation (seconds of feedback) and `full` only on release, without editing the global skill.
- **Project maintainer** — wants to define project-specific test commands per type in their own repo (cwd), with the ability to add new types beyond the minimum set.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CLI parameter:** `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (and the `/skill:test` entry point) accepts `--type <value>` with values `smoke`, `unit`, `full` (minimum). `full` is the default when `--type` is omitted. Unknown values produce a clear error listing the allowed values. Help text documents the parameter.
2. **Type-to-command mapping is driven by a local CWD extension when present:** The runner looks for a local test-skill extension in the **current working directory** (the invoking project) — the extension mechanism provided by SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0. When a local extension is present, it is expected to define the commands for each of the minimum types (`smoke`, `unit`, `full`). The global skill delegates to the local definition in that case.
3. **Local extension may define more:** A local extension may define additional types beyond the minimum (e.g. `dev`, `e2e`, `quick`) and additional testing strategies. The global skill must accept and dispatch any locally-defined type, not just the three minimum values.
4. **Fallback when no local extension exists:** When no local extension file is found in cwd, the global skill falls back to sensible defaults / existing convention detection for the three minimum types.
5. **Existing behaviour preserved:** Bare invocation with no `--type` remains `full` and preserves the existing full-suite contract (caching per SA-0MSIU5HFI0024D7W, scope handling per SA-0MT6BYQHB008DOGC, `.pi/test-config.json` override per SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61, triage flow, and audit Skill cache consumption). No regression to current `run_tests.py --json/--summary` usage.
6. **Tests for the new behaviour** and documentation updates. Follow the `test-config.json` extension precedent already used by the skill (see `skill/test/SKILL.md` suite-command resolution).

## Constraints

- The local extension file location and format must follow the convention introduced by SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 — this work item **depends on** (blocked by) that parent. Do not invent a separate discovery path.
- The global skill must not hardcode project-specific commands (e.g. Tableau Card Engine vitest profiles). Project specifics belong in the local extension, discoverable at cwd.
- Backwards compatible: existing callers with no `--type` flag see no behaviour change.
- The skills remains usable from any cwd, including when invoked with `--worklog-dir` / prefix-to-sibling resolution.

## Existing state

- Runner: `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — resolves `full_suite_commands(project_root)` from `.pi/test-config.json` or conventions (pytest / node / npm-test). No typed entry point.
- Docs: `skill/test/SKILL.md` documents the full-suite workflow and cache contract.
- Parent: SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 (in_progress, idea) will provide the per-project extension loading mechanism. This child is blocked until that mechanism lands.
- Real-world motivator: Tableau Card Engine audit CG-0MT5XO7DI0066QCT timed out on the full-suite auto-execute inside the audit runner; the correct AGENTS.md fast track is `npx vitest run --project unit ...` (seconds). A local extension would have let `skill/test --type unit` do the right thing.

## Desired change

1. **Parent first:** Land SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 so CWD extension discovery is available.
2. **Then this child:** Add `--type` to `run_tests.py` + `SKILL.md`, wire delegation to the local CWD extension when present, implement fallback defaults, include clear errors for unknown types, add tests and docs.

## Key Files

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — add `--type smoke|unit|full` (default full), local CWD extension delegation, fallback defaults
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — document --type, the minimum types, the local extension contract, and the release-only vs implementation guidance
- `skill/test/tests/test_run_tests.py` — tests for --type parsing, defaults, local extension delegation, unknown-type errors, backwards compat

## Risks & assumptions

- Assumes SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 exposes a stable CWD extension file path/format for skills to consume. If the parent changes the convention, this child must follow it.
- Risk: local extension defining incomplete type maps (e.g. missing `unit`) — runner should fail with a clear diagnostic, not silently run full.
